description: Attack the n=512 B=640 cluster (4 of 12 shapes, ~7.8k us each = the largest absolute geomean cost), the one SM-SATURATED regime (640 matrices >> 148 SMs, so compute/panel-bound, NOT latency-bound like n=2048/4096). A sibling found panel-vs-trailing OVERLAP wins ~13% but only via a BANNED non-default CUDA queue; the REMOTE-SAFE version is a FUSED SINGLE-KERNEL look-ahead: factor panel j+1's leading block and run panel j's wide trailing update inside ONE persistent kernel on the default queue (no extra queue), so the panel latency hides under the trailing GEMM via warp specialization / async SMEM pipelining (cp.async) rather than cross-queue concurrency. One CTA per matrix at B=640 fills the GPU. FP32 panel (TF32 fails the gate); per-matrix TF32/FP32 trailing as in parent. Keep all other n exactly as parent (b050aa33). Single default queue only — do NOT use a non-default CUDA queue and do NOT write or obfuscate the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Trial 6 (FINAL): in-kernel LOOK-AHEAD fused n=512 (brief's mechanism). Per panel p, ALL warps update the lead block [jp+NB,jp+2NB); then M_PW=8 PRODUCER warps factor panel p+1 (PTX bar.sync 1) WHILE M_CW=8 CONSUMER warps run panel p's wide trailing GEMM on [jp+2NB,N) (bar.sync 2) -- disjoint H cols, between two all-CTA barriers. Single default queue, no 'stream', remote-safe. Validated PASS (22 tests+3 guards, n=512 factor resid 1.35). Geomean 10447us (SLOW benchmark mode this session; n1024 anchor ~21000 vs parent fast-mode ~9000). SAME-MODE verdict: look-ahead 10447 vs parent 9090 = 1.15x WORSE; n=512 28191 vs parent cuBLAS 17669 = 1.60x slower; vs SERIAL fused (24149 same mode) look-ahead 1.17x slower. Look-ahead is NET-NEGATIVE at SM-saturated n=512 B=640: double-buffered V => 3->2 CTAs/SM, lost inter-CTA occupancy already hid the panel (matches brief-19's 1.3%). Serial fused best fused variant but 1.37x slower than parent cuBLAS (WMMA trailing<cuBLAS, per brief-5).

Trial 1: FUSED single-kernel QR for n=512 SERIAL baseline (no look-ahead). One persistent CTA/matrix (grid=3*148, grid-stride over B=640), blocked Householder NB=16: panel FP32 (warp-shuffle reflectors) + Gram-WMMA compact-WY T (3xTF32) + trailing C-=V T^T V^T C via 2xTF32 WMMA strip-mined (STRIP=256), ALL in ONE kernel on the default queue. Removes per-panel cuBLAS launch storm + global panel<->trailing barriers (nsys: 1 kernel launch vs ~33 in parent). n!=512 EXACTLY parent. Ported in-tag brief-5 best (94789bd9) qr_megakernel single-CTA path as the look-ahead foundation. All 22 tests+3 guards CLEAN (n=512 factor resid 1.35<<20). geomean 14355 in VERY-slow benchmark mode (n1024 anchor 32096). ncu: 3 CTAs/SM, 60% occ, 40 regs, stalls 32.7% CTA-barrier + 30.4% SMEM-scoreboard (latency-bound). Serial fused ~1.3-1.4x slower than parent cuBLAS (brief-5: 11.9k vs 7.8k).

Trial 2: IN-KERNEL LOOK-AHEAD overlap (warp specialization, named barriers), M_PW=4. Per panel p, ALL warps update lead block [jp+NB,jp+2NB); then 4 PRODUCER warps factor panel p+1 (bar.sync 1) WHILE 12 CONSUMER warps run panel p's wide trailing GEMM [jp+2NB,N) (bar.sync 2) -- disjoint H cols, between two all-CTA barriers. Remote-safe in-kernel equivalent of cross-queue overlap (single default queue, no 'stream'). Double-buffered V (Vcur/Vnext), one W strip, STRIP=192. All 22 tests+3 guards CLEAN. n=512 cond2 28074us NORMAL mode (n1024 anchor 20955==parent run) vs parent 17669=1.59x slower; geomean 10461. ncu: occupancy DROPPED 60%->47% (3->2 CTAs/SM), regs 40->64; duration unchanged vs serial -- overlap exactly offset by lost occupancy.

Trial 3: force __launch_bounds__(512,3) on the look-ahead to cap registers (64->~40) and try to recover 3 CTAs/SM. MEASURED REGRESSION: n=512 cond2 36717us (normal mode, n1024 anchor 20998) vs trial-2 28074 (+31%). The register cap SPILLS the heavier look-ahead kernel (genuinely needs 64 regs); SMEM (~80KB w/ double-buffered V) still caps at 2 CTAs/SM regardless. Confirms double-buffered-V look-ahead is STRUCTURALLY limited to 2 CTAs/SM at NB=16 (2 full-height V buffers=66KB > 56KB for 3/SM). geomean 11511. Reverted launch_bounds to 2.

Trial 4: revert launch_bounds to 2; sweep producer warps M_PW 4->8 (8 producers/8 consumers). n=512 cond2 28200us (normal, n1024 anchor 20946) == trial-2 PW=4 28074 (within noise). PW (overlap balance) does NOT move the result -- look-ahead is bound by occupancy (2 CTAs/SM from double-buffered V), not producer/consumer balance. geomean 10480. No PW tuning rescues the look-ahead at SM-saturated n=512 B=640.

Trial 5: clean SAME-MODE A/B of the SERIAL fused (trial-1 design, single-buffer V, 3 CTAs/SM) vs look-ahead. Restored serial qr_mega512 (byte-identical to trial 1, validated PASS) and benchmarked in the CURRENT normal mode (n1024 anchor 20927). RESULT: serial fused n=512 cond2 24149us, geomean 9921. SAME-MODE: serial fused 24149 vs LOOK-AHEAD 28100 (trial 2/4) => look-ahead 1.16x SLOWER than serial (double-buffer 3->2 CTAs/SM; lost inter-CTA occupancy > intra-CTA overlap at saturated B=640). Serial fused 24149 vs PARENT cuBLAS 17669 => fused 1.37x slower (WMMA trailing < cuBLAS GEMM).

BUILT the brief's in-kernel look-ahead for n=512 and MEASURED it across 6 trials. It is CORRECT (all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN every trial; n=512 factor resid 1.35<<20) and REMOTE-SAFE (single default queue, warp-specialized PTX named barriers bar.sync, zero 'stream' substring, no cudaStream/non-default queue). HEAD=1c5139be (look-ahead, the brief's mechanism).

MECHANISM BUILT: fused single-kernel QR for n=512, one persistent CTA/matrix (grid-stride over B=640), blocked Householder NB=16, ALL in one kernel on the default queue (panel FP32 warp-shuffle reflectors + Gram-WMMA compact-WY T 3xTF32 + 2xTF32-WMMA strip-mined trailing). Look-ahead: per panel p, ALL warps update the lead block [jp+NB,jp+2NB), then M_PW PRODUCER warps factor panel p+1 (named bar 1) WHILE M_CW CONSUMER warps run panel p's WIDE trailing GEMM on [jp+2NB,N) (named bar 2) -- disjoint H columns, between two all-CTA barriers. Double-buffered V (Vcur/Vnext). This is the exact remote-safe in-kernel analog of brief-19's banned cross-queue overlap.

MEASUREMENTS (benchmark ran SLOW/normal mode all session -- n1024 anchor ~21000 vs parent fast-mode ~9000; bimodal, GPU-contended; ALL comparisons below are SAME-MODE so mode-independent):
- PARENT cuBLAS n=512 cond2 = 17669us; geomean 9090 (my baseline run).
- SERIAL fused (trial 1/5, single-buffer V, 3 CTAs/SM) n=512 = 24149us; geomean 9921 => 1.37x slower than parent.
- LOOK-AHEAD fused (trial 2/4/6, double-buffer V, 2 CTAs/SM) n=512 = 28100-28200us; geomean ~10460 => 1.60x slower than parent AND 1.17x SLOWER than the SERIAL fused.
- PW sweep (4 vs 8): no change (look-ahead bound by occupancy, not producer/consumer balance).
- launch_bounds(,3) to recover 3 CTAs/SM: REGRESSED to 36717us (register SPILL -- kernel needs 64 regs).

ROOT CAUSE (ncu-confirmed): at SM-saturated n=512 B=640 (640 CTAs >> 148 SMs), the serial panel->trailing dependency within one matrix's CTA is ALREADY hidden by the OTHER ~3 matrices' CTAs co-resident on the SM. The look-ahead's double-buffered V (66KB for 2 full-height NB=16 V buffers) drops occupancy 3->2 CTAs/SM, REMOVING that inter-CTA hiding; the intra-CTA producer/consumer overlap only replaces it (duration unchanged serial->lookahead), and the net is the occupancy LOSS. This independently matches sibling brief-19's measurement that cross-queue overlap won only 1.3% at n=512 (saturated => little overlap room). Separately, EVERY fused variant is >parent because the in-kernel WMMA trailing < cuBLAS's GEMM at this shape (brief-5's 19-trial finding: fused 11.9k vs parent 7.8k fast-mode).

VERDICT for the manager: the brief's in-kernel look-ahead is net-NEGATIVE at n=512 specifically because the shape is SM-saturated (the overlap it provides is already provided for free by inter-CTA occupancy, and double-buffering destroys that occupancy). The serial fused is the better fused variant but still loses to parent cuBLAS by 1.37x.

OPEN DIRECTIONS I did NOT reach:
1. SINGLE-BUFFER look-ahead to keep 3 CTAs/SM: have the CONSUMER read the current panel's V from global H (only the NB*NB diagonal block needs an SMEM unit-lower-trapezoid mask; the tall part is raw H reflectors) -- eliminates the Vcur SMEM buffer so only Vnext (33KB) is double-counted, possibly restoring 3 CTAs/SM WITH overlap. This is the one variant that could vindicate the look-ahead (decouple overlap from occupancy loss); risk = extra global V traffic on an already memory-bound kernel.
2. The look-ahead is structurally RIGHT for the LATENCY-BOUND large-n shapes (n=1024 B=60, n=2048 B=8) where the GPU is UNDER-occupied -- exactly where brief-19 measured the cross-queue overlap winning 13%/10%. My brief forbade touching n!=512, but a fused look-ahead routed to n=1024/2048 (few matrices, occupancy NOT saturated, so double-buffer costs nothing and overlap is pure gain) is the natural high-EV follow-up.
3. tcgen05 (Blackwell 5th-gen MMA + TMA) for the in-kernel trailing -- the only path to make the fused trailing match/beat cuBLAS GEMM (brief-5 left it unbuilt); would lift the 1.37x serial-fused floor that caps ALL n=512 fused approaches. High complexity + remote-safety re-check needed.
4. STRIP sweep on the look-ahead (only 192 tested) and NB>16 (needs bigger WMMA tiles) were not swept.
The n=512 fused floor (serial 24149 same-mode) sits above parent's 17669, so absent (1) or (3) landing a >1.37x in-kernel speedup, the parent's separate-panel+cuBLAS n=512 path remains faster. Keep the look-ahead alive for the under-occupied large-n shapes (direction 2) where its premise holds.
